pages.text: "Sonu, here's our house!" Mina, a handspan taller, stood two wooden dolls on a lower step. Round-bellied little Sonu placed pebbles beside them. River water slowly approached.
Mom came down with laundry and called, "Water's coming. Come up." "A little longer! The house isn't finished." Mina did not even look up from the dolls.
Water lapped over a white stone set in the step. One doll floated away. "My doll!" Mina's voice trembled.
Mom held both children's hands and climbed to a dry higher step. "Losing your doll is upsetting. But let's get ourselves up first."
Mom pointed to the covered white stone. "The water's reached here. Stop playing today and go home." Mina held Sonu's hand.
Mina looked back once toward the doll. Mom offered a hand. "Leave the rest, too." Empty-handed, Mina took hers.
All three climbed. Each time Sonu went up a step, Mina matched the pace beside them. Mom stayed close.
They reached the yard. Below, the play steps were underwater. Mina held Sonu's hand tightly.
"What about the dolls?" Sonu asked. "We'll look with Mom later. Let's stay home now," Mina answered.
Mom sat both children on her lap. "You climbed well." Sonu leaned on Mina, and Mina snuggled into Mom's arms.
